headlines.article_text: Shopify Q3 2026 earnings: Revenue, GMV miss estimates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Shopify reported Q3 earnings before the bell on Tuesday. The e-commerce platform beat earnings expectations but posted revenue just below LSEG estimates. Gross merchandise volume and subscription gross profit missed estimates. In this article SHOP Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 2:59 02:59 Shopify president Harley Finkelstein: Shopping through AI channels is 'growing quite quickly' Squawk on the Street Shares of e-commerce platform Shopify fell 7% on Tuesday after the company missed estimates on subscription gross profit and gross merchandise volume. Shopify reported before the bell Tuesday and posted adjusted earnings of 49 cents per share, topping LSEG estimates of 46 cents per share. Overall, quarterly revenue of $3.74 billion came in just below LSEG estimates of $3.75 billion. Shopify said it sees revenue growth in the "low thirties" range year over year for the fourth quarter, versus LSEG estimates of 32.1%. Gross merchandise volume, which came in at $119.15 billion, missed analyst estimates of $120.03 billion for the quarter, according to StreetAccount. Subscription gross profit also missed estimates by nearly $20 million, coming in at $661 million compared to StreetAccount estimates of $680.3 million. Merchant gross profit beat estimates. Shopify president Harley Finkelstein called the GMV results "consistent" and "durable" in comments to CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Tuesday, and noted it was the thirteenth consecutive quarter of GMV growth above 20%. "We're really proud of the print, and we're going to keep building for the long term and ignore the noise day to day," Finkelstein said. Subscription revenue of $836 million also missed analyst estimates of $848.1 million, according to FactSet. Merchant revenue beat estimates. The partnership allows Muse to browse and purchase items on Shopify's platform within the Muse app and allows customers to check out with Shopify's payment service, Shop Pay. Finkelstein addressed concerns about potential pricing pressure as AI agents negotiate prices and cost compare on behalf of users. "We're not seeing that prices are being lowered," he said. Instead, Finkelstein said AI agents are driving new traffic to Shopify's business and are helping consumers find new brands and products. "Brands like the Tin Can phone, a screenless phone for kids, are seeing incredible success because of agentic-based commerce, where a consumer is being very specific and using very merit-based results and using Shopify catalog. It is presenting these great products to consumers that there's no way they would have found otherwise." Finkelstein acknowledged some economic pressure on consumers heading into the holiday season, but said businesses are optimistic and agentic shopping could have a breakthrough moment. "I do think this is the first holiday season where AI-assisted shopping capabilities will become mainstream, especially with the rise of personal agents," he said. headlines.article_text: Bill Ackman warns of 'casino' stock market trading Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Bill Ackman, the founder of Pershing Square Capital Management, said he worries that the stock market is "broken," due to the rise of speculative trading that has led to wild price swings. The volatility has created opportunities for the hedge fund to buy companies it considers high quality at discounted prices, he said, pointing to Microsoft, Amazon, Visa, Mastercard and Netflix. But he warned that short-term speculation can hurt investors. Pershing Square CEO Bill Ackman speaks on CNBC's "Squawk Box," Nov. 3, 2026. CNBC Bill Ackman told CNBC on Tuesday he worries that the stock market is broken, saying the rise of speculative trading is leading to wild price swings thanks to the amount of leverage in the system. "Every number of days, I feel like markets are broken," Ackman said on CNBC's " Squawk Box ." "Stocks trade at prices that make no sense to me. Yes, it's good if you're a long-term investor and you can buy at a stupid price. I don't think it's good for the country generally." "We're back to the casino-type markets when there was 95% leverage," he added. "I don't think that's inherently good for the economy, for society, and it's leading to these massive moves in stocks." It also bought Alphabet when the stock moved "massively" following ChatGPT's launch, he said. But the billionaire investor worries that the rise of one-day leveraged vehicles, perpetual futures and sports betting is dangerous for investors who are treating the stock market as a get-rich-quick scheme — an attitude that could have disastrous consequences. "It's good for us long term — 'us' being Pershing Square," he said. "I don't think it's good for the country." U.S. commercial revenue topped government for the first time, but the company closed $1.5 billion in TCV in the segment, up 11% from last year. In Q2, Palantir closed a record $2.1 billion worth of TCV in the segment, which was up 153% from the prior year. Investors will "no doubt be looking for evidence in subsequent quarters that 11% growth in U.S. commercial TCV bookings is a fluke of duration and not something structural," a Piper Sandler note from Monday said. "We believe that is the case and demand for PLTR's solutions still very much outstrip supply." In a Tuesday note, Goldman Sachs analysts noted that the company attributed some of this to shorter contract durations. "The key will be converting shorter duration contracts into longer duration commitments, which Palantir has done successfully in the past," the analysts wrote. Revenue nearly doubled from a year ago and blew past $2 billion for the first time, Palantir said in its earnings report. Palantir stock chart. Apple's earnings The iPhone maker reported better-than-expected revenue in its fourth-quarter earnings, but fell short of estimates on iPad sales and issued a margin forecast that disappointed investors. Apple 's statement marked the first earnings report since John Ternus took over as CEO from Tim Cook in September. The stock fell more than 2% on Tuesday. The company is reckoning with a global memory crunch and a scramble for computer components. Memory costs were higher this quarter than in the June period, the company said Monday. Despite the price surge, Ternus said Apple had just capped off its "best fiscal year ever." He told CNBC's MacKenzie Sigalos that Apple's growth came despite supply constraints and foreign exchange headwinds. "The concern is profitability," said Violeta Todorova, senior research analyst at Leverage Shares. "Management pointed to memory as the main pressure, together with the cost of rolling out Siri AI. Memory shortages are also expected to limit Mac and iPad supply, as demand has run ahead of plans." Apple shares have risen 25% in 2026, ahead of other big tech names, but that premium leaves "little room for disappointment," Todorova added. Some managers at the entertainment giant have been asked to reduce costs by up to 20%, according to the people, who asked not to be named because they were not authorized to speak publicly. It marks the latest round of layoffs since CEO Josh D'Amaro took the reins earlier this year. The update comes after separate plans in April to cut as many as 1,000 employees , predominantly in the marketing department, and in September to cut about 300 employees , many in human resources and technology divisions. "We remain highly focused on reducing costs across the enterprise to create incremental capacity to invest for growth and are evaluating a variety of levers," D'Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston wrote in an Aug. 5 letter to shareholders . "We are mid-stream in this work and will provide future updates on our progress." Disney introduced plans in August for an early retirement program for some employees. "This is one of several actions we're taking to reshape our organization, including involuntary staff reductions that have already begun in some areas and will continue into next year," Chief People Officer Sonia Coleman wrote in a letter to employees on Aug. 24. Disney had about 231,000 employees as of the close of its fiscal year 2025, which ended in September of that year, according to the company's annual financial report. Disney is not the only entertainment company looking to reduce costs. Netflix said in a memo last month that it would lay off roughly 6% of its workforce . headlines.article_text: Yum Brands (YUM) Q3 2026 earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Yum Brands beat Wall Street's quarterly earnings estimates and its revenue was in line with expectations. Taco Bell's same-store sales declined as a cyclospora outbreak tied to lettuce served at its restaurants weighed on traffic. During the quarter, Yum completed its divestiture of Pizza Hut. In this article YUM Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A woman leaving Taco Bell on July 28, 2026, in Washington,DC. The Washington Post | Getty Images Yum Brands on Tuesday reported earnings that beat expectations, but a cyclospora outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce at Taco Bell weighed on the company's same-store sales growth. However, Yum said Taco Bell, which the company considers a "growth engine" for its business, has since rebounded. "Since the end of September, Taco Bell U.S. has been outpacing the [quick-service restaurant] industry on same-store sales growth," Yum CEO Chris Turner said in a statement. Taco Bell's same-store sales are up about 1% so far in the fourth quarter, CFO Ranjith Roy said on the company's earnings conference call Tuesday. In the last four weeks ended Friday, same-store sales have risen 3% compared with the year-ago period. Here's what the company reported compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: $1.56 adjusted vs. $1.49 expected Revenue: $2.05 billion vs. $2.05 billion expected Yum reported fiscal third-quarter net income of $1.62 billion, or $5.92 per share, up from $397 million, or $1.41 per share, a year earlier. Excluding gains from its divestiture of Pizza Hut and other items, the restaurant company earned $1.56 per share. Net sales rose 4% to $2.05 billion. During the quarter, Yum completed its divestiture of Pizza Hut. It closed the sale of the pizza chain's business in mainland China to Yum China on Aug. 7 and sold the rest of Pizza Hut to LongRange Capital on Sept. 1. The company's third-quarter results include Pizza Hut up until those dates. Excluding Pizza Hut, Yum's same-store sales were flat for the quarter as Taco Bell weighed on the company's overall results. Taco Bell's same-store sales declined by 4% as diners temporarily pulled back on visits due to the foodborne illness outbreak . Yum executives previously said the weekend of July 18 saw the most severe impact to sales, but trends have improved since then. Taco Bell's most loyal customers returned faster, Yum said, thanks in part to weekly Tuesday deals for loyalty program members after the cyclospora outbreak took over headlines. Traffic from "medium" and "light" customers has bounced back to about 95% of prior levels, while visits from "heavy" users is back to normal, Roy said. To attract more casual diners, Taco Bell has been relying on star power, like a collaboration with pop star Olivia Rodrigo on a pink-colored Mountain Dew Baja Blast. Outside of the U.S., Taco Bell's much smaller international business reported same-store sales growth of 5%. KFC's same-store sales ticked up 1%, helped by system sales growth in China and Europe. The U.S., now the chicken chain's third-largest market, saw system sales shrink 6% in the quarter. Like Restaurant Brands International's Popeyes , KFC has struggled in the U.S. amid a wave of new competitors and more budget-conscious consumers. Its home market represents only about 5% of KFC's operating profit, but it remains a symbolically important part of the business for Yum investors. During the quarter, KFC U.S. launched popcorn chicken, which sold out in many restaurants. However, Yum said the limited-time menu item was not enough to offset the successful Hot & Spicy Wings and Potato Wedges promotion during the year-ago period. Globally, KFC is trying to become "the most modern chicken QSR ," Turner said on the company's earnings conference call. To achieve that lofty goal, he said the chain will roll out buzzy promotions, a new brand identity, and a wider menu that includes upgraded sauces and more beverages.
